title: Query.AddTimeFilter produces a time filter that does not match the equivalent parsed query: different String() output...

source.license_note: Real upstream victoria PR #8991; ACBench task derived from its regression test + fix.

task.summary: Query.AddTimeFilter produces a time filter that does not match the equivalent parsed query: different String() output and a different max timestamp.
task.instructions: Fix the defect in the logstorage package so the failing regression test passes without modifying any test.
task.acceptance_notes: FAIL_TO_PASS must pass; do not edit *_test.go.

code_fault.description: Query.AddTimeFilter sets the filterTime maxTimestamp directly to end and formats stringRepr as "[start, end]" with a space, so it does not match the inclusive end-time rounding and spacing applied when parsing the same _time:[start,end] filter from a query string.

ops_fault.description: Programmatically adding a global time filter yields a query that is not equivalent to parsing the same _time range, causing inconsistent serialized queries and a wrong effective end timestamp.
localization_keywords: filterTime maxTimestamp set directly to end
stringRepr formatted as [start, end] with a space
missing getMatchingEndTime call on end timestamp
inclusive bracket end-time rounding not applied
serialized form must match parsing logic
repair_keywords: format stringRepr as [start,end] without the space
make AddTimeFilter output match parsed _time filter

visible_context.issue_text: Adding a global time filter through Query.AddTimeFilter produces a query that is not equivalent to parsing the same _time:[start,end] range: the serialized query string differs and the effective maximum timestamp is wrong.
error_logs: query produced by AddTimeFilter does not match parsed equivalent
visible_context.notes: Real upstream regression; diagnosis injected as upstream ops context.
